findings.defect: On the pad the frosting tanks are covered with flat, hard-edged cut-out patches (rounded rectangles and wedges on the 0.2 x 0.5 m skin grid) filled with a fixed screen-door stipple. The MERIDIAN lettering, roundel, LOX stencil and CAUTION CRYOGENIC placard under them become grey ghosts; from the pad cameras the tank lettering reads as broken dots. A row of white specks pokes out along the lower ring of the corrugated intertank band (the shell cutting through the corrugation valleys). It reads as peeling masking paper, not frost, and it is on the vehicle in the first view of the game.
findings.realReference: Frost on a LOX tank is a continuous matte white coat over the whole cryogenic barrel between the frost lines, with soft vertical streaks, thicker ridges on weld lands and stiffener rings and a feathered edge at the frost line. Markings under thin frost keep sharp edges and lose contrast. There are no polygon outlines and no dot texture; on white paint the visible change is gloss to matte plus a slight blue-white lift.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/parts/stage.ts:356-429: the rime is a separate shell cut from frostPatch() on the lathe grid (hence polygon edges) and emitted with PoseOpts.fade = rimeCover (0.72) * k, i.e. permanently dithered coverage in the mesh G-buffer shader (src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:130-134). The screenshots freeze the blue-noise offset (src/render/core/renderer.ts:618, noiseOffset [0,0] when deterministic), so the dither never resolves; even resolved it is a 72 % blend of a hard-edged shell. The shell stands a few mm proud, less than the corrugation amplitude at the intertank.
findings.fixDirection: Remove the dithered shell. Put frost into surface shading: a frost weight per vertex times a texture-space noise threshold (centimetre fbm, streaked along the axis, soft smoothstep edge), driving albedo to white, roughness to 0.8+, the foam normal map and clearcoat to 0. The last needs the core mesh shader's frost term to scale clearcoat in gbufferExtra (file a render-core request; the hand-off notes the term cannot do it today). Keep the frost line as a soft gradient over 0.3 m. If any shell stays, give it fade 1 and stop it short of the corrugated bands.

findings.defect: The launch mount is dressed with primitives. Rainbirds are bright red faceted cones on plain grey posts (one fills the foreground of the clamp view). Hold-down clamps are flat slab 'tombstones' with one pin, a yellow arm carrying a row of grey squares, and gusset plates rendered as stipple. The tail service mast is a plain grey box on a slab post with three bent pipes ending on a bare plate. The mount stair is a pure black zig-zag ribbon with no treads or rails. The mount itself is a concrete box on four square piers and its deck is an untextured flat blue-grey plane. Next to engine bells that do carry detail, these read as placeholder art at a glance.
findings.realReference: Real mounts (LC-39 ML, SLC-41, Starbase OLM): rainbirds are large galvanised or oxide-red pipe risers with elbows, flanges, bolt circles and fan nozzles; hold-down posts are massive welded or cast steel with pivoting arms, hydraulic cylinders, blast shrouds and bolted bases; service masts have hoods, hinge frames and bundles of flex hoses; stairs have stringers, grating treads, handrails; decks are scorched, rust-streaked steel or refractory concrete with drain slots and cable trays.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/site/pad.ts:367-376 (rainbird = rod + frustum in a flat red paint), the launch-mount block of pad.ts:280-366 (box girder, piers, stair as untextured dark beams), the 'pad.clamp' generator in src/render/vehicle/parts/structures.ts, and the swing-arm umbilical plates in src/render/vehicle/site/tower.ts. The complex has 160 k triangles at LOD0 against 1.1 M for the vehicle; none of it is spent here.
findings.fixDirection: Model these as hardware: rainbird = riser pipe with flange, elbow, flared fan head and support struts in galvanised steel; clamp = boxed weldment with ribs, hinge pin and lugs, hydraulic actuator, arm with a pad and proper diagonal hazard stripes from the decal sheet, bolted base plate; service mast with hood, hinge and hose bundle to the vehicle's umbilical plate; stairs with stringers, treads and rails using the grating material; give the deck the concrete or steel texture set plus blast scorch through the grime mask. Drop the dithered gussets (see the LOD finding).

findings.defect: Any part whose projected size is within 15 % of a LOD switch is drawn as two complementary stipple patterns. The bell extensions and rims of the M-1 and M-2 engines are rings of dots (red and white pixels of whatever is behind show through); the sooted bell interiors sparkle white along the rim; the whole interstage-2 cone at 40 m is salt-and-pepper with a doubled, garbled MERIDIAN decal and a black rectangle beside it; clamp gussets are stipple. This is visible in 8 of the acceptance stills at ordinary framing distances.
findings.realReference: A LOD change must not be visible at all: a shipped renderer either swaps within one or two frames behind TAA or cross-fades for a fraction of a second after the switch. No surface is ever left half-transparent because of the distance the camera happens to be at.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:20 and 649-660: LOD_FADE_BAND = 0.15 is a band in projected SIZE, so a camera parked in the band keeps both LODs dithered at 50 % indefinitely. The stills also freeze the blue-noise offset (src/render/core/renderer.ts:618), so TAA cannot average it. Package side: engine lodPixels [200, 44] (src/render/vehicle/parts/engine.ts:381) and the default [220, 60] on stage structures put the switch exactly at the size these parts have in the standard 9 to 40 m views, and LOD1 differs from LOD0 in decal regions and bands, so even a resolved blend ghosts.
findings.fixDirection: Package: lower the first switch for hero parts (engines about 90-110 px, interstages and skirts about 120 px) and make LOD1 keep the same silhouette, material bands and decal regions as LOD0 so a blend is invisible. Core request: replace the size band with a time-based cross-fade (about 0.25 s after the switch, with hysteresis), and keep the noise animated or accumulate jittered frames in deterministic captures so screenshots show what TAA resolves. Then re-shoot these eight views and check a slow dolly through the switch distance for ghosting.

findings.defect: The glowing heat shield is one flat colour: 255,210,126 at the centre and at both edges (red channel clipped), no radial gradient, no hotter shoulder or stagnation region, none of the ablator's texture or gore pattern showing through, the six compression pads glowing as identical flat blobs, and a bloom fringe only a few pixels wide. It looks like an orange paper disc stuck under the capsule.
findings.realReference: An ablating shield at about 1900 K is deep orange to orange-red, brightest at the stagnation region and the shoulder (offset by the angle of attack), darker toward the lee edge, with the char pattern, gap lines and flecks of ablating material visible; brightness varies by more than a factor of two across the face and the hottest zone blooms.
findings.likelyCause: The shield is one instance with one temperature (heatShield.surfaceTemp via the capsule pose in src/render/vehicle/parts/capsule.ts and src/render/vehicle/vesselFeature.ts); the mesh shader adds blackbody(T) * 0.85 uniformly (src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:181-182), which clips in the tonemapper at the space exposure. The hand-off lists this as known.
findings.fixDirection: Give the temperature spatial structure: either split the shield into 3-4 concentric rings plus the shoulder as separate models with their own temperatures (as the engines' hotA / hotB bands already do) driven by a profile that depends on the angle of attack, or ask the core for a per-vertex heat weight (a mask channel scaling the instance temperature). Multiply the emission by the albedo texture's luminance so char and gaps read, and bring the 1900 K colour to orange (about 255,120,30 before bloom) so it does not clip.

findings.defect: Night lighting is omni point lights with no shadows and no beam. At the pad the ground is one smooth radial pool; the rocket, masts, poles and tower cast no shadow at all, a pole standing beside a floodlight is shadowless, and the vehicle is lit evenly top to bottom. Chrome pipe runs and thin lattice members break into rows of sparkling dots under the point lights. On the lander the lamps light the ground and legs while the body stays pure black, yet the top deck rim of the descent stage and one vertical seam strip are lit on the far side of the hull: light passing through the ascent stage (light leak). Glints on the black ascent stage read as random white scratches.
findings.realReference: Pad xenon floodlights are aimed beams: the vehicle is brilliant white against black, with several hard, long shadows of the stack, tower and masts radiating across the apron, bright where beams overlap and visible beam cones in haze. A lander's lights throw hard leg and engine-bell shadows on the ground, and regolith bounce softly lights the underside and lower body.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/siteFeature.ts:230-237 and the vessel feature register every lamp as LocalLight kind 'point' (src/core/contracts/render.ts:428: no cone, no shadow). src/render/vehicle/parts/lander.ts:336-344 places two omni lights of range 60 m 0.9 m below the descent-stage rim and :524-527 one of range 40 m 1.1 m off the ascent lamp; with no occlusion they light surfaces on the other side of the hull.
findings.fixDirection: File a render-core request for spot lights (cone angle, falloff) and shadows for at least the 2-4 brightest local lights (one small shadow map each, or reuse a cascade slot at night). Until then: aim by geometry (put each light well in front of its lens along the beam axis and cut the range so it cannot reach behind the hull), shorten the lander lights to about 15 m and add a dim ground-bounce fill under the vehicle. For the sparkle, widen roughness on chrome pipes and lattice members in the far LODs.

findings.defect: The foil does not read as foil. (a) From 10-15 m under a low sun the silver blankets are a black-and-white camouflage mosaic (pixel values 13 next to 250) and the gold is blotchy brass. (b) Close up the crinkle is an obvious Voronoi 'cracked mud' cell pattern, flat cells with raised ridges, identical on gold, silver and black. (c) In orbit light the silver blanket shows cloudy fbm noise and the highlight is cut dead at a panel seam: bright on one panel, black on its neighbour. (d) The tank lobes are perfect cylinders with flat matte tops; no tape, tie-downs, overlap or sag.
findings.realReference: Aluminised Kapton on the Apollo LM and current landers hangs in loose sheets: long soft wrinkles radiating from fasteners and taped seams, pillows between tie points, reflections that are stretched streaks of sun and ground. A panel stays recognisably gold or silver across its area instead of breaking into black-and-white noise, and neighbouring panels overlap with visible tape.
findings.likelyCause: public/assets/vehicle/mli_n.png (1024 px facet-built normal map, 1.1 m tile) on a smooth lathe surface with metallic 0.85-0.9, roughness 0.38-0.4, anisotropy -0.6 (src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:79-81): mirror-like facets under a black sky are either on or off, and nothing widens the lobe as the cells shrink below a pixel. The seam step is the anisotropy tangent (or UV) flipping between adjacent panel strips in src/render/vehicle/parts/lander.ts.
findings.fixDirection: Put the large wrinkles into LOD0 geometry (displace the blanket with long creases and pillows between tie points) and bake a normal map of directional creases at lower amplitude instead of cells. Raise base roughness to about 0.5 with variation, and bake normal variance into the roughness mips (Toksvig or LEAN) so distant foil converges to a broad sheen rather than sparkle. Make tangents continuous round each body. Add taped seams, grommets and panel overlaps.

findings.defect: The back shell reads as masonry: tiles about 0.2 m across with wide dark joints and roughly one beige tile in eight make the capsule, and especially the apex tunnel, look like a stone kiln. Round every window, the hatch and the KESTREL marking there is a rectangular patch whose tile grid is laid at a different angle and offset, so tiles are sliced mid-way along the patch border (clearly visible as boxes around both windows). The marking itself is a plain pale rectangle that wipes the tiles out like a sticker. The 'tape' strips down the cone carry the quilt normal map and look like a twisted drill bit with sawtooth highlights.
findings.realReference: Back-shell tiles (Orion, Shuttle) butt with gaps of about a millimetre, filled flush; beyond a few metres the joints almost vanish and the shell reads as one surface with faint tone variation, often with aluminised tape over it. Close-out tiles round a window are cut to fit and their outline follows tile edges, never a rectangle slicing through tiles. Markings are painted across tiles with the joints showing through. Joint tape is a smooth reflective strip.
findings.likelyCause: public/assets/vehicle/tile_albedo.png / tile_n.png (64 tiles, 1.44 m tile, dark wide joints and strong tone steps), material 'tile-white' in src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:77. Close-outs: src/render/vehicle/parts/capsule.ts:279-325 gives the rectangular grid block round each opening planar UVs square to the opening. Marking: opaque decal rectangle (capsule.ts:527-532). Tape: capsule.ts:598-605 builds 35 mm boxes in 'blanket-silver', which uses quilt_n at a 0.8 m tile.
findings.fixDirection: Re-bake the tile set with joints of 1-2 mm equivalent (thin, mid-grey, mostly a normal and roughness feature), much weaker tone variation, and fade the joint contrast by mip. Keep the course UVs through the opening blocks and only re-lay the ring of close-out tiles next to the frame, ending on course joints. Composite markings over the tile texture (bake the marking into a tile-backed atlas region or multiply the tile joints into the decal). Give the tape its own smooth aluminised material.

findings.defect: Markings are broken by the geometry they sit on. On the stringer skirt of M-2 the flag is chopped into a bar-code of separate coloured strips, 'LH2' and 'LOX' are split between letters and CAUTION CRYOGENIC is cut into four pieces, because the stringers over the decal carry plain paint; from 15 m it reads as coloured blocks. On smooth paint every decal shows as a rectangle: the sun streak on M-1 steps brighter and sharper inside the flag and M-1 rectangles. Access-door outlines on the interstage and the fairing petal render as a rectangle of irregular dots. On the white room the panel battens run across the LC-1 sign (the C reads as an O) and straight across the porthole glass.
findings.realReference: Livery is paint: it runs unbroken over stringers and corrugations, has exactly the gloss and orange peel of the paint round it, and has no visible rectangle. Access panels show a continuous hairline gap with a row of fasteners. Signs and windows sit on top of cladding battens or the battens stop at them.
findings.likelyCause: Decals are opaque atlas rectangles cut into the lathe skin (hand-off deviation 5; decalRegion in src/render/vehicle/parts/common.ts:28, used at stage.ts:71), while stringers() (common.ts:60, called at stage.ts:204-210 and structures.ts:210) are laid over the whole band in the skin material. Material 'decal' (src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:102) has roughness 0.46 and clearcoat but neither paint_n nor paint_orm, so its highlight differs from 'paint-white'. accessDoor (common.ts) draws its gap as sub-pixel geometry. Battens in src/render/vehicle/site/tower.ts are placed without regard to the sign and porthole.
findings.fixDirection: Either keep stringers out of decal regions or, better, give stringer faces the decal UVs where they cross a decal region so the marking continues over them. Give the decal material the paint normal and ORM maps and the same roughness and clearcoat as the paint it sits on, and make the atlas background exactly the paint colour. Draw door gaps as a normal-map or AO groove (or a gap at least a pixel wide at LOD0 with a coarser LOD without it). Stop battens at signs and openings.

findings.defect: Sun shadows of thin structure are poor. On the trench wall beside the mount stair a shadow is drawn as a checkerboard halftone. Shadow edges on the white elevator shaft and tower columns are film-grain speckle. Lattice-mast and tower shadows on the ground are blocky, hatched noise near the camera and at 300 m are reduced to a faint dotted trace or nothing (150 m masts and floodlight poles with no shadow, while the same masts have shadows in pad-arms-retracted.png: a pop with distance). The shadow under the ground pipe runs is a ragged smear of blobs that reads as rubble. On the lunar slab thin strut shadows dissolve into dots along their length.
findings.realReference: Hard sunlight gives lattice structures crisp, continuous lattice shadows near the base that soften evenly with distance from the caster (penumbra about 1 % of that distance); a pipe on sleepers has a thin continuous shadow line; shadows of tall masts stay visible from any distance at which the mast is visible.
findings.likelyCause: Members are thinner than a shadow texel beyond the first cascades (radii 12, 60, 300, 1500 m in src/render/core/shadows/cascadeMath.ts:17), pipe runs cast only into cascades with texels up to 0.35 m (NEAR_SHADOW_TEXEL, src/render/vehicle/site/types.ts:46), cascade-to-cascade transitions are dithered (src/render/core/shaders/chunksLighting.ts:514-515) and the PCSS rotation uses the same blue noise, all frozen in the stills (renderer.ts:618). Shadows are cast by LOD1 / LOD2, whose lattice members differ from LOD0.
findings.fixDirection: Give lattices and pipes a dedicated shadow proxy: members thickened to at least 1.5 texels of the cascade they are drawn into (or a solid slender prism with reduced opacity for the far cascades) so the shadow never drops out; cast pipe-run shadows into one more cascade with a proxy box. Re-shoot with animated noise to see what the dithered cascade blend and penumbra really resolve to; if grain remains, ask the core for a blended (not dithered) cascade transition on static casters.

findings.defect: The lander hovers over the slab in every 'on the ground' acceptance view. The foot pads show their lit undersides with no contact shadow, and each pad's shadow (an ellipse with the strut's line attached) lies metres away from the pad: from the pad's on-screen size and the 16 degree sun the pads are about 0.6 m above the slab. So ground contact, the pad-on-surface look and the leg shadows have never actually been pictured. The slab itself is a smeared low-resolution concrete plane under a flat grey band.
findings.realReference: A landed pad sits in the surface: its rim touches or sinks a few centimetres, its shadow starts at the pad and the gap under the dish is black. The brief asks for the lander 'on a flat ground slab' with no floating.
findings.likelyCause: labs/vehicle/labSim.ts:214-224 and 253 place the lowest PartDef.bounds.yMin on the slab (legs -1.15 m), while the feet are drawn where legPose puts them for the stroke compression the scene's legs module reports (src/render/vehicle/parts/lander.ts:543-551, 717); pad bottom is contact point -0.7 minus radius 0.4, shortened further by the compression. Lab-only: in the game the simulation places the vessel by contact.
findings.fixDirection: In the lab place the vessel by the legs' contact points for the current deploy and compression (or force compression to the static value and derive the height from legPose), then re-shoot the five lander ground views and check contact from a low camera. Add an assertion that the lowest drawn pad vertex is within 2 cm of the slab.

findings.defect: Open steel grating is an opaque slab. Looking up the stack, the underside of every swing-arm walkway and tower platform is a solid jet-black plank; nothing of the sky or structure shows through, and they would cast solid shadows. The edges of the same walkways sparkle with white specks (edge-wear metal aliasing along the beam chords).
findings.realReference: Bar grating is 70-80 % open: from below it is a fine grid with the sky and the structure above visible through it, and it throws a dappled, half-strength shadow.
findings.likelyCause: Material 'grating' (src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:67) is an opaque albedo and normal texture; the mesh system has no alpha test (hand-off deviation 5). The sparkle is the edge-wear vertex mask (masks.r, meshSystem.ts:156-159) turning thin beam edges into bare metal that aliases.
findings.fixDirection: Request alpha-tested (cutout) materials in the mesh system, with alpha-to-coverage or the existing dither for the cutout and a matching shadow pass; until then build LOD0 gratings as real bearing bars (instanced flat bars every 30-40 mm are affordable on the few walkways near the camera) and use a 50 % dithered plane for far LODs and shadows. Reduce edge wear on members thinner than a few pixels.

findings.defect: Brushed steel shows scan-line banding. The anisotropic highlight on the interstage is built from blocky horizontal stripes with stair-stepped ends that repeat down the surface, and on M-3's black steel section the streak is crossed by regular horizontal lines. The box fairing on the hull in the close-up sits in a blotchy dark speckle (unresolved shadow or AO noise round its base) and has one face rendered as a bright white strip.
findings.realReference: Brushed stainless has a continuous, fine, slightly irregular grain: the highlight is a soft streak whose edges feather into countless hair-thin scratches, with no visible rows, steps or repeat, plus faint handling marks and weld tint.
findings.likelyCause: tools/vehicle/bake-textures.ts:46-63: the brushed height field is 0.00003 m, so brushed_n.png is flat (2 distinct R values, 4 distinct G), and all visible grain comes from brushed_orm roughness, which is constant along u ('each scratch is a line of constant v'): perfectly straight 1.5 mm rows on a 0.4 m tile, magnified by the anisotropic lobe (materials.ts:54-57).
findings.fixDirection: Bake real scratches: many short strokes of finite length with small angular jitter (about 1-2 degrees) and varied depth, at 2-3 scales, into both the normal map (enough amplitude to span at least 6 bits) and roughness; use a larger tile (1.5 m or more) or two detail scales so no repeat shows; keep anisotropy but lower it slightly so the texture, not the lobe, carries the grain.

findings.defect: Sub-pixel geometry aliases into dots at 720p. The lightning catenary is a dotted black line across the sky in the look-up view (it is a clean line in the 1440p perf frames). The forward-skirt stringers of M-3 break into dashed white lines; weld seams on M-1 are dashed; the cable tray on the tank is black speckle; at 800 m pipe runs are rows of dots. The fillet of the boost cover carries a single-pixel white specular spark that will flicker in motion.
findings.realReference: A thin wire or seam seen from far away is a faint continuous line that fades out with distance; it never breaks into beads. Specular highlights on tight fillets are short soft streaks.
findings.likelyCause: Member thickness below one pixel with no coverage-based fade: lodPixels switch on the bounding-sphere size of the whole model (a 400 m catenary or a 30 m stage is always 'large'), so thin members stay at LOD0 thickness (src/render/vehicle/site/tower.ts:596 lodPixels [2500, 900] for the wires). The spark is the clearcoat lobe (clearcoatRoughness 0.14) on a fillet narrower than a pixel; the Kaplanyan term in the mesh shader is capped at 0.18.
findings.fixDirection: Split long thin structures into segments instanced separately so each picks its LOD by its own distance, and in every LOD keep members at least about 1.2 px wide at the switch distance, with reduced contrast (darker or lighter toward the background) instead of thinner. Remove weld beads and stringer detail from geometry beyond the distance where they are under a pixel and carry them in the normal map there. Raise clearcoat roughness on small-radius fillets or widen the specular AA kernel for clearcoat.

findings.defect: The stages alone read as smooth CG tubes. M-2 at 40 m is a uniform flat orange cylinder with about ten soft dark smudges at near-regular spacing (the 9.6 m foam tile repeating) and no form; M-3 is a featureless cream cylinder between two bands. Under M-2 the inside of the aft skirt is a flat, untextured primer-green band with no frames or stringers, the vacuum bells are plain smooth dark cones and the thrust-structure blanket is a perfectly regular diamond lattice. The M-2 dome inside the interstage is a bare disc with three thin pipes. Close up the foam is an even popcorn bump that turns to noise at grazing angles.
findings.realReference: Spray-on foam tanks (SLS core, Delta IV, Centaur) show machined spray-pass ribbing, darker UV-aged patches with irregular outlines, hand-sprayed close-outs at flanges and brackets, pressurisation lines, cable trays, access covers and visible barrel weld lands; skirts show frames, stringers and harnesses inside; vacuum nozzles show stiffener bands, weld seams and heat tint.
findings.likelyCause: 'foam-orange' / 'foam-white' with one 2048 px map at a 9.6 m tile (src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:70-74; foam_albedo.png has only about 50 distinct levels per channel), normal detail at one scale; inner skirt in plain 'primer' without structure (src/render/vehicle/parts/stage.ts:325 adds stringers only above the equator); LOD1/LOD2 of the engines drop the bell bands.
findings.fixDirection: Add a second, non-repeating macro layer to the foam (vertex colour or a 30-40 m tone map) and directional spray ribbing in the normal map; add geometry breaks (raceways, feedline fairings, brackets, close-out ridges) along the barrels; frame and stringer the skirt interiors; keep the stiffener bands and seams on the vacuum bells in LOD1.

findings.defect: Soot and char do not look burnt. The sooted M-1 skin is soft grey vertical bands with a metallic sheen that stop dead at ring seams and panel lines (a darker panel next to a lighter one across a weld), so it reads as brushed aluminium plates. The charred shield (ablator fraction 0.58) is the pristine tan with brown radial streaks, like stained wood; the pristine face has a fine corduroy line pattern. The 'charred' back shell is almost unchanged apart from blurred grey smears near the rim.
findings.realReference: Flown boosters carry matte black-grey soot, heaviest aft, streaked along the airflow with sharp clean boundaries where frost or hardware protected the paint. A flown ablative shield is dark grey to black, mottled, with ash-grey patches and flow streaks toward the lee shoulder; the back shell is scorched brown-black on the windward side.
findings.likelyCause: Soot is a per-vertex mask (masks.b) times the instance soot (src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:160-163), so its resolution is the lathe grid and each panel strip ramps on its own; the clearcoat stays on under soot. Char is a vertex-mask blend toward a brown tone in src/render/vehicle/parts/capsule.ts with the same ablator albedo.
findings.fixDirection: Make soot weights continuous across panel and ring boundaries, add a streak noise in texture space, and have soot remove the clearcoat (same core request as frost). Give char its own dark, mottled albedo and roughness (second texture or stronger blend) keyed by ablatorFraction, with flow streaks toward the shoulder, and scorch the windward back-shell tiles.

findings.defect: Clipping and loose ends. The red deluge main and a chrome line run straight through both walls of the support building with no collar or valve pit. The crew-arm stays are two thick grey tubes rather than cables, and truss, tunnel and white room have no contact shading at joints. Tank-farm pads at 800 m are outlined by a hard dark line, and the apron ends as a razor-thin sheet on the ground. In the last three staging frames the jettisoned escape tower stands inside the top of the ascent stage with its motor against the capsule's heat shield (debris drifting through other vessels in the scripted sequence), which makes the sequence look broken.
findings.realReference: Pipes enter buildings through sleeves or turn into valve pits; guy stays are thin cables with turnbuckles; slabs have kerbs, a shoulder and soil build-up at the edge; separated hardware never overlaps other hardware.
findings.likelyCause: data/defs/sites/ka-lae-lc1.structures.json routes the pipe run through the building footprint (hand-off, known weaknesses); stays in src/render/vehicle/site/tower.ts use a beam-sized radius; labs/vehicle/labSim.ts gives jettisoned vessels a slow drift along the stack axis with no clearance, and tests/browser/vehicle/staging.spec.ts advances only 1.5 s per stage.
findings.fixDirection: Re-route the main round the building or end it in a valve house with wall sleeves; thin the stays to cable gauge with end fittings; add a kerb and gravel shoulder to slabs; in the lab give the escape tower and other debris lateral separation velocities so they clear the stack before the next stage.

findings.defect: The lab environment hides what the models will look like and adds artefacts of its own. Whites never reach white: sunlit white paint (albedo 0.8) is 138-147 of 255 in the space views and 182 on the pad, so the vehicle is grey everywhere; the day sky is slate (90,104,134, down to 65,77,107 overhead) over a single flat brown plane with a knife-edge horizon and no haze. A small black blob hangs in the day sky at the same direction in both tower views and the 1440p frame (azimuth about 237, elevation about 24 degrees): the lab's Moon drawn unlit. Nothing here has been judged under the real atmosphere and terrain (the hand-off says so). Run note: the functional suite was re-run for this review on 2026-11-11 (10 passed, 1 skipped ad-hoc) and rewrote the 68 spec views; the two perf frames and the 27 adhoc-* files are from 2026-11-10 and were viewed as they are.
findings.realReference: Sunlit white paint photographs at 85-95 % of display white with highlights clipping; a tropical noon sky is bright and saturated near the zenith, pale at a hazy horizon; the daytime Moon is a pale, lit disc.
findings.likelyCause: labs/vehicle/labEnv.ts (analytic sky 5200-11500 cd/m2, ground one colour) and the lab exposure, which sits about a stop under for sunlit hardware; labs/vehicle/main.ts:196 gives createLabPlanetFeature a map only for the root body, so the Moon has none.
findings.fixDirection: Shoot the pad, tower, apron and night views in the integration lab under the real sky, atmosphere and terrain (the black frames the builder got there need a diagnosis, not a retreat), set exposure so sunlit albedo-0.8 paint lands near 0.8 of display white, and either light the lab Moon or leave it out. Treat every material judgement in this package as provisional until that is done.
